To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
differential cross sections for electron emission are not simply scaled versions of each other.

1) differential cross section scaling is possible in the case of ionization by intermediate and high energy structured projectiles; and 2) the scaling is not possible for low energy structured projectiles.

the differential cross section for the ejection of an electron from a heavy ion-atom collision can be scaled with the projectile velocity, and the cross section for the emission of a given energy can be scaled with its velocity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and application of theoretical models to describe the ionization and excitation of atoms by charged particles.
the study of the differential ionization cross section for the interaction of heavy ions with atomic targets.
the development of a unified theory of heavy ion-atom interactions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the cross sections for ionization of atoms by heavy ions are very sensitive functions of projectile charge, velocity, and nuclear size.
no single method can be used to describe all the data.
no single model or scaling law is applicable over the whole range of energies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the scaling laws are not as general as previously believed.
, although the scaling laws are not as general as those for atomic targets, the scaling is still useful in many instances.

the high energy approximation, which assumes the incident particle to be a point charge, provides a reasonable description of the cross sections for the outermost shells of atoms, but fails for the inner shells of heavy atoms.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, for a given projectile, the cross section for emission from a given shell is a function of the energy and charge of the target, but is not strongly affected by the charge of the projectile.
the scaling laws which are appropriate to the description of ionization by high energy electrons and protons do not apply to the ionization of atoms by intermediate and high energy heavy ions.
, in the case of outer shell ionization of heavy atoms by heavy projectiles at intermediate to high energies, differential cross sections are well approximated by a simple scaling law.
